newsitem.title: UK: CWS to ban sales of alcopops from June 16.
newsitem.headline: CWS to ban sales of alcopops from June 16.

text.p: The Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) said on Friday that its retail group is to ban the sale of alcoholic soft drinks knows as alcopops at its 1,200 licenced stores from June 16.

The Co-operative Retail Trading Group, which accounts for around 60 percent of Co-op alcoholic drink sales, said in a statement the decision was the "result of growing concern over the consumption of these drinks by under-18 (year-olds)."

"As responsible retailers, we feel the time has come to act, given the concern expressed by our own customers, pressure groups and the government," said Bill Shannon, head of corporate affairs for CWS, which co-ordinates buying and marketing for the group.

While the decision was taken "with reluctance", Shannon said, "We believe these drinks are designed specifically to appeal to young people and are, in fact, largely consumed by under-18s, who cannot legally buy them".

UK Interior Minister Jack Straw on May 16 called for an urgent inquiry into the consumption of alcopops. A decision made just one day after alcopop makers were condemned as "grossly irresponsible" by a judge after he heard how a 14-year-old boy got drunk on alcoholic lemonade and cider and then burned down a school.
Shannon said he hoped other retailers would follow its lead.
Among the brands being dropped are: Britain's best selling alcopop Hoochers Hooch, made by Bass Plc ; Two Dogs made by Merrydown Plc and Whitbread Plc's Vanilla Heist and Lemon Jag.
Total alcopop sales are worth around 265 million pounds ($431.9 million) a year.
